San Telmo is the oldest neighborhood in Buenos Aires, Argentina, renowned for its 19th-century colonial architecture, cobblestone streets, antique markets, and deep roots in the history of tango.
Exploring this historic district on foot allows you to trace the evolution of the city from a muddy colonial port to the vibrant cultural heart it is today.

evidence.title: Two to Tango: A San Telmo Self Guided Walking Tour
evidence.snippet: San Telmo is the oldest neighbourhood in Buenos Aires, and its cobblestone streets hold enough history to fill several lifetimes. On this self-guided walking tour, you'll trace how sailors, slaves, immigrants, and tango singers turned a muddy colonial outpost into the soul of the city. You'll also discover how a yellow fever epidemic, two British invasions, and millions of Italian immigrants each left their mark on this single neighbourhood. The tour starts at Basílica de San Francisco, where a …

evidence.title: San Telmo Walking Tour and Market Experience – Buenos Aires
evidence.snippet: Experience the heart of Buenos Aires with a walking tour through San Telmo, the city's oldest neighborhood. Explore cobblestone streets lined with 19th-century architecture and uncover stories of colonial history and Argentine heritage. Enjoy the vibrant atmosphere as you learn how immigration shaped local culture and see the neighborhood come alive with music and art during the famous Sunday street fair. - Visit the iconic San Telmo Food Market and discover its rich history and unique features.…

evidence.title: San Telmo Essential Tour: Tango, Market \u0026 Museums
evidence.snippet: Walk San Telmo with an English teacher and know the oldest and most fantastic neighborhood in BA. We'll meet at Adolfo Alsina 400 (double-check apart from the app's map) at Basilica San Francisco de Asis, and we will also see the iconic Farmacia la Estrella, the oldest pharmacy in BA, then head to Convento Santo Domingo, where the English invasions occurred. We´ll see icons of Argentinean culture, such as “Mafalda” and the smallest house in Buenos Aires. The iconic tango bar \"El Viejo Almacen\"…

evidence.title: San Telmo \u0026 Market Tour
evidence.snippet: On the San Telmo tour we will walk the oldest streets of Buenos Aires, learning about colonial BA and the crucial moments of Argentine history. Cobblestone streets and beautiful XIXth century buildings will frame our tour talking about immigration into the city and the creation of the modern local culture, including Mafalda (the most famous little girl from Buenos Aires), the traditional San Telmo Food Market and the unique Sunday street Fair. We will see the market and the fair, explaining all …

evidence.title: Buenos Aires: Casa Mínima Guided Tour in San Telmo
evidence.snippet: Begin your journey through Buenos Aires’ history with a guided visit to Casa Mínima, the city’s narrowest house, tucked away behind a facade just 2.3 meters wide. This intimate space is a living relic of San Telmo, preserving the neighborhood’s oldest myths and traditions. As you step inside, you’ll discover how the house’s walls have witnessed the transformation from the era of slavery to the vibrant origins of tango, offering a rare glimpse into the lives that shaped this iconic district.Your …
